title: Earth mover distance sketching complexity
formal: Determine, up to universal constant factors, the minimum sketch length \(s(n,c)\) for approximating planar earth mover distance for every integer \(n\geq2\) and real approximation factor \(c\geq1\). Inputs are subsets \(A,B\subseteq[n]^2\) of equal cardinality, with unit mass at each occupied grid point, and \[\operatorname{EMD}(A,B)=\min_{\pi:A\to B\ \mathrm{bijection}}\sum_{a\in A}\|a-\pi(a)\|_1.\] Each set must be encoded independently using the same public randomness. From the two \(s\)-bit encodings the decoder must return \(\widehat d\) satisfying \(\operatorname{EMD}(A,B)\leq\widehat d\leq c\operatorname{EMD}(A,B)\) with probability at least \(2/3\) for every fixed pair.
why: EMD sketching asks how much information must be retained to compare geometric mass distributions without keeping the original data. Sharp tradeoffs would clarify the limits of metric compression and the distinction between embeddings, sketches and full-input transport algorithms.
status_note: The full tradeoff and highlighted constant-approximation/polylogarithmic-size question are open in the 2011 source. The bounded later-work search through 14 September 2026 found no matching characterization for this exact subset and public-coin model. Full transportation-norm and L₁-distortion results have been checked separately and do not by themselves certify a resolution.

progress.text: Theorem 1.1 provides sublinear-size sketches with constant approximation when its parameter is fixed.
Indyk records the tradeoff question and specifically asks for constant approximation with polylogarithmic bit length.
Sketching/embedding equivalences imply nonconstant resources for the full transportation norm, with a different input domain and threshold task.
The planar L₁-distortion gap is closed in the STOC publication; this is not a general sketch-decoder lower bound.

importance.reason: A central compression problem for optimal transport, with a consequential unresolved constant-approximation/polylogarithmic-space regime and a full information-versus-accuracy tradeoff.

sentences: Each planar grid subset must be compressed independently before the other input is available.
The decoder uses the two bit strings to estimate the minimum Manhattan-cost matching of equal-size sets.
The target is the optimal tradeoff between sketch length and multiplicative approximation, with constant success probability for every fixed pair.
Known embedding and full transportation-norm results do not automatically characterize arbitrary decoders for these subset sketches.
Sharp bounds would establish how much information optimal-transport comparisons must retain.

definitions: Here \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\|(x,y)-(u,v)\|_1=|x-u|+|y-v|\); grid spacing and point mass are both one. Empty sets are allowed and their distance is zero. There are no repeated points, arbitrary real weights or bounds on cardinality beyond \(|A|=|B|\leq n^2\). A length-\(s\) scheme for parameters \((n,c)\) is a probability space of public seeds \(R\), encoders \(L_R:2^{[n]^2}\to\{0,1\}^s\), and decoders \(D_R:\{0,1\}^s\times\{0,1\}^s\to\mathbb R_{\geq0}\), with all relevant events measurable. The estimate is \(D_R(L_R(A),L_R(B))\). The seed is independent of the inputs and available to both encoders and the decoder. Seed length and local computation are unrestricted and not charged; this is information-theoretic sketch length in bits, not streaming update time or the dimension of a real vector. The decoder knows \(n,c,R\), but receives no input-dependent information beyond the two sketches; any stored cardinality is charged. The same encoder works for both inputs. Success is required for each fixed pair chosen independently of \(R\), not simultaneously for all pairs under one seed or against adaptive exposure of the seed. When \(A=B\), success requires estimate zero. Define \(s(n,c)\) as the least integer \(s\geq0\) admitting such a scheme; it is finite because the entire \(n^2\)-bit incidence vector can be stored. The displayed interval fixes the usual one-sided multiplicative convention explicitly; it is not an additive-error guarantee.
answer_criterion: Provide a noncircular positive rate \(g(n,c)\) and a complete Lean-checked proof that universal constants \(a,b>0\) and \(n_0\) satisfy \(a g(n,c)\leq s(n,c)\leq b g(n,c)\) for every \(n\geq n_0\) and every \(c\geq1\). The upper bound must supply schemes with the stated probability and bit length; the lower bound must cover all allowed, possibly nonlinear, public-coin schemes. Constants and \(n_0\) cannot depend on \(c\), so varying approximation regimes and logarithmic factors must be accounted for. A single upper bound, a linear-embedding lower bound alone, or the answer for only one fixed approximation factor does not determine the requested tradeoff.

context_blocks.text: Indyk’s 2011 question asks for the sketch-length/approximation tradeoff and highlights the possibility of constant \(c\) with \(s=\operatorname{polylog}n\). The card retains that full tradeoff and specifies the grid, masses, randomness and approximation convention.

A sketch must be computed without seeing the other set. The decoder then estimates one transport cost from two compressed descriptions. A fast algorithm that reads both complete inputs can exploit information that the sketch decoder does not have.

Andoni, Do Ba, Indyk and Woodruff prove that, for any fixed \(0<\varepsilon<1\), a sketch of polynomially sublinear grid-size dependence can obtain approximation \(O(1/\varepsilon)\). Their Theorem 1.1 uses \(O(n^\varepsilon)\) integer coordinates of polynomial magnitude; for sets this converts to \(O(n^\varepsilon\log n)\) bits. Thus constant-factor approximation is possible with more than polylogarithmic space in the stated construction.

Andoni, Krauthgamer and Razenshteyn prove that the full planar transportation norm cannot have both constant approximation and constant-size distance-threshold sketches. That norm allows general signed real mass vectors; the theorem neither identifies this subset-only bit tradeoff nor rules out polylogarithmic sketches.

The published STOC 2026 lower bound of Gartland and Ostrovskii closes the planar \(L_1\)-distortion gap for transportation cost spaces at order \(\log n\). An embedding theorem is not a theorem about every arbitrary decoder of two finite sketches, so this result does not automatically resolve the present question.

The number of grid locations and the number of occupied points are different parameters. Here the grid side length is the parameter and every equal-size pair is covered. Likewise, replacing the one-unit point masses by arbitrary weighted distributions would enlarge the input family.
